title: A double convex lens immersed in a liquid: how its power in dioptres varies with the liquid's refractive index
summary: A double convex glass lens (n = 1.5, R = 20 cm) sits in a tank whose liquid index n_L you change. Its rays converge, pass straight when the lens vanishes at n_L = 1.5, then diverge, while a plotter draws the power: 1/f is a curve (A), the optical power n_L/f a straight line (B) - the official key accepts A or B.
subject: Physics
topic: Power of a thin lens immersed in a liquid - lens-maker's formula in a medium, optical power n_L/f against 1/f
subtopics: Refraction at a spherical surface: surface power (n2 - n1)/R
Thin lens in a medium: optical power = sum of the surface powers = (n_g - n_L)(1/R1 - 1/R2)
A lens vanishes when n_L = n_g and changes from converging to diverging when n_L > n_g
Two definitions of power in a medium: 1/f (a hyperbola in n_L) and n_L/f (linear in n_L)
concepts: Each surface of the lens bends light by (n_g - n_L)/R, so the bending depends on the index difference with the liquid
Optical power n_L/f = 10(1.5 - n_L) D: a straight line through 5 D, 0 and -5 D at n_L = 1, 1.5, 2 - plot (B)
1/f = 10(1.5/n_L - 1) D: a curve (hyperbola, concave up) through 5 D, 0 and -2.5 D - plot (A)
At n_L = 1.5 there is no refraction: f is infinite and the power is zero, so plots that diverge there (C, D) show f, not power
The official key accepts A or B because the two plots are the two standard definitions of power in a medium

methods: Solved independently: surface powers (n_g - n_L)/R added give n_L/f = 10(1.5 - n_L) D, a straight line (B); the lens-maker's formula in the liquid gives 1/f = 10(1.5/n_L - 1) D, a curve (A); both zero at 1.5, so C and D (divergent there) are out
sympy: optical power 2(n_g - n_L)/R and 1/f = power/n_L; values 5, 0, -2.5 and 5, 0, -5 D; convexity and linearity; plot matching gives exactly A and B
Exact Snell's-law ray trace through the two spherical surfaces (no paraxial formula): f = 20 cm in air, 78.2 cm in water, -40 cm at 2.0; the traced 1/f matches plot A and n_L/f plot B
ABCD matrices (reduced angles): system power = n_L/f at every liquid
Every option audited: A (1/f) and B (n_L/f) accepted; C and D diverge at 1.5 where the power is zero (they behave like f); D also has the wrong sign in air
